episode: The Collegium of Lumen — Expanded Entry and GM Secrets

changes.name: The Collegium of Lumen
changes.entry:
The Collegium of Lumen is [entity:9614806|Fogport]’s great school, licensing authority, research house, patent office, and monopoly-holder for sanctioned Lumen magic. It dominates the upper end of the [entity:9663320|Pales]: a fortified compound of pale stone walls, copper roofs, slate towers, condenser chimneys, elevated bridges, and blue-white lamps burning behind rain-streaked glass.

From the street, it seems to rise forever.

This is deceptive.

Old engineers claim the Collegium descends farther below sea level than its tallest tower rises above the Pales. Beneath its public courts lie drowned foundations, pressure shafts, sealed lecture vaults, pumping halls, flooded galleries, and machinery that has been running so long that no living professor can explain its original purpose. The Collegium denies having “lower levels.” It refers instead to sub-foundational facilities, which is how a person knows there are lower levels.

To ordinary citizens, it is simply the Collegium: a place where serious people in dark coats learn to make the impossible obey diagrams, gauges, legal doctrine, and carefully punched parchment.

Students study mathematics, natural philosophy, civic safety, fog chemistry, wand operation, Lumen pressure, intellectual property law, and the dreadful art of calculating where a spell’s cost will fall. A good Lumenist can mend a bone, arrest a fire, clean poisoned blood, or ward a factory door. A bad calculation can leave a whole neighborhood cold, unlucky, and full of exhausted fog.

The Outer Collegium

The public may enter only a narrow outer portion of the institution: the registry hall, an infirmary, supervised demonstration rooms, a licensing court, and a long arcade of approved suppliers.

Here, applicants wait beneath brass signs while clerks inspect seals and measure handwriting. Families bring injured relatives to be treated by student physicians. Independent [entity:9663318|Luminati] renew their ribbons, pay fines, argue over patents, and buy authorized replacements for damaged Reels.

It is possible to spend an entire day in the outer Collegium without seeing a single actual spell.

The inner courts, extraction works, scriptoria, tower galleries, laboratories, dormitories, archives, and underground facilities are closed to everyone without a student seal, staff ribbon, or a very powerful invitation.

Wardens are polite. This does not make them gentle.

The Reel Monks

The Collegium’s most revered workers are the Reel Monks: cloistered craft-scholars who illuminate, calculate, hand-punch, test, repair, and certify the parchment Reels used by the Luminati.

Their work resembles sacred manuscript-making crossed with industrial instrument manufacture. A proper Reel may contain thousands of tiny holes, cuts, wax marks, repairs, and annotations. Each bears a maker’s mark small enough to hide beneath a thumbnail. An excellent Reel can be passed down for generations. A damaged one may make a healer close the wrong thing.

The Monks are not universally beloved. They decide which experimental Reels are safe, which are illegal, which must be confiscated, and which are “not yet suitable for public understanding.”

They also keep the best mistakes.

The Grand Reel Galleries

Beneath the public halls lie the Grand Reel Galleries: locked corridors of colossal parchment programs wound around drums taller than houses. The reels turn slowly behind iron grilles while machines clatter, sigh, and occasionally scream in a language of steam.

Some are said to govern civic wards, hospital systems, tram protections, weather barriers, flood pumps, and Fogport’s emergency lighting.

Others are classified beyond even most faculty.

One gallery is rumored to contain a Reel that has been running since before the Catastrophe. Another is said to be blank, yet its drum turns whenever someone dies inside the Pales. A third was sealed after its reader began producing written examination results for students who had not yet enrolled.

The Collegium calls all of these stories nonsense.

It has posted guards outside every door involved.

The Deep Collegium

The deeper levels are where the Collegium becomes strange.

Below the old foundations, the air grows wet, warm, and metallic. Pipes disappear into black water. Elevator cages descend farther than the city’s sewers. There are pressure doors with no visible handles, lecture chambers built beneath the waterline, and abandoned laboratories where every surface has been painted white to make the stains easier to identify.

Officially, these levels contain pumps, storage cisterns, archives, condenser foundations, and old infrastructure.

Unofficially, they contain failed research, confiscated artifacts, creatures altered by uncontrolled Lumen exposure, and experiments too expensive—or too embarrassing—to destroy.

Students dare each other to steal a brass maintenance token and ride a service lift downward until the attendant asks them a question they cannot answer.

Most return before that happens.

A Monopoly with Manners

The Collegium trains Lumenists, but employs relatively few of them. Once licensed, a wizard usually becomes an independent contractor and must purchase their own Reels, inspections, seals, replacement parts, and renewals from the institution that certified them.

This keeps the Collegium wealthy, powerful, and deeply resented.

It insists that its monopoly protects Fogport from reckless magic. Its critics note that sanctioned wards, magical lighting, weather protections, and emergency services appear first within the Pales and other wealthy districts, while dockworkers and fog-harvesters are left with cold rooms, bled fog, and warning pamphlets.

The Collegium responds that civilization requires expertise.

Its critics answer that expertise has become a toll gate.

What It Wants

The Collegium’s stated purpose is to make magic useful, lawful, and safe.

That is true.

It also consumes more Lumen than any other institution in Fogport. Its greatest operations draw from somewhere. The Pales has been pale for generations. The nearby fog trade has suffered. Gardens struggle. People who live near major extraction works speak more softly and sleep less well.

The Collegium says these are manageable civic costs.

Some professors believe it is building a citywide system that will finally make Fogport safe from storms, fire, disease, and unlicensed magic.

Others suspect it is trying to power something much older beneath the city.

And a few, very quietly, are afraid that whatever lies at the bottom of the Collegium has begun to answer its calculations.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Collegium of Lumen
posts.entry:
Use This as a Menu, Not a Master Plan

The Collegium is a powerful, divided institution—not an all-seeing villain and not the explanation for every mystery in Fogport. Pick one immediate need, one buried secret, and one internal opponent when it enters play. Leave the rest as rumors, competing theories, or future material.

Fate Aspects

  • There Is a Form for That
  • Safety at a Price Someone Else Pays
  • Every Miracle Has a Meter
  • The Deep Levels Are Still on the Budget
  • A Monopoly with Manners

Fate Troubles

  • The City Is Running on Borrowed Breath: the Collegium’s public works really do keep parts of Fogport alive, making blunt sabotage morally costly.
  • Every Department Protects Its Own Disaster: faculty conceal mistakes, rival theories, dangerous prototypes, and colleagues who should have been dismissed years ago.
  • The Pales Pays First: when extraction goes wrong, residents, students, servants, and nearby workers suffer before senior decision-makers do.
  • Procedure Can Be Weaponized: a correct permit, forged seal, technical appeal, or missing comma can change who is allowed to act.
  • The Deep Does Not Stay Filed: water, pressure, old machinery, and buried research periodically intrude into respectable upper-world business.

Possible Immediate Needs

  • A Grand Reel is chewing itself apart and will shut down a hospital ward, tram signal system, or flood pump unless an unlicensed person reaches a sealed maintenance route.
  • A student examination cohort has vanished into a lawful but forgotten sub-foundational field exercise. The Collegium wants them recovered quietly before parents, newspapers, or the Civic Vigilance learn where they were sent.
  • A fog-harvester strike has cut off a reagent supply. A practical dean needs someone who can negotiate outside Collegium etiquette—or steal a shipment back without starting a district riot.
  • A Reel Monk has discovered a subtle defect in a widely sold safety Reel. Recalling it would ruin the Collegium’s reputation; concealing it will injure people.
  • A flooded archive is losing irreplaceable research every tide. The official rescue team cannot enter because the archive is technically not supposed to exist.

Possible Buried Secrets

Choose one when it becomes useful; none need be true until discovered through play.

  • The Inverse Boiler: the deepest condenser is not drawing Lumen from Fogport. It is holding back a pressure of raw Lumen rising through flooded stone. The Collegium’s extraction program is partly a safety valve, and partly making the problem worse.
  • The First Curriculum: the earliest Reel Monks did not invent their notation. They copied it from a sealed pre-Catastrophe machine beneath the foundations. Modern Reels work because nobody has dared change the language they barely understand.
  • The Human Cost Ledger: a small accounting office knows exactly which blocks lose heat, luck, sleep, and health after major operations. Its records prove that “manageable civic cost” is a deliberate policy choice.
  • The Lower Faculty: several professors officially died, retired, or resigned. In truth they remain alive in a submerged lecture complex, maintaining an experiment that cannot be stopped without consequences.
  • The Blank Gallery: the allegedly blank Grand Reel records possibilities rather than events. It produces examinations for students before enrollment because it is measuring who will become useful to the machine.

Internal Factions

  • The Civic Engineers genuinely want safer streets, hospitals, and flood control; they will make ugly compromises to keep systems operating.
  • The Patent House values monopoly, licensing fees, and political protection above discovery. Its villains are mundane, polished, and extremely well documented.
  • The Reel Monks fear uncontrolled innovation but know more about the old machinery than they admit. They are capable of both genuine moral courage and terrifying conservatism.
  • The Lower Faculty believe a dangerous project must continue because stopping it would be worse. They may be right.
  • The Unlicensed Alumni are former students, expelled researchers, and failed licensees who know the institution’s blind spots but are not automatically heroes.

Hooks for Byl and Lott

  • A Reel Monk offers Byl a legal license examination in exchange for an impossible favor: enter a silent dry patch below the Collegium where Lumen refuses to behave. The Monk is more interested in Byl’s wild card magic than the favor.
  • Lott is hired as ordinary muscle for a midnight archive salvage. The crates are light going down and far too heavy coming back; one begins politely asking him to put it somewhere warmer.
  • A student’s forged permit bears Byl’s old street-magician alias. The Collegium assumes he is part of a smuggling ring and sends a courteous investigator before the Civic Vigilance sends Korch.
  • A neighborhood clinic offers to repair an injury for free if Byl retrieves a stolen medical Reel. The thief is using it to save dockworkers, and the Reel is the only thing keeping a sick child alive.
  • A service lift opens beneath the Pales with three soaked faculty members inside. They insist it has only been five minutes. Their paperwork says they left the Collegium thirty-two years ago.
  • A Grand Reel begins printing playing-card symbols among its punch marks. The Collegium wants Byl to explain them; Byl should not be able to.
  • A Luminati rival attempts to solve an industrial problem by draining Lumen from Nine Spoons. Byl and Lott can stop the operation, exploit it, or force the Collegium to admit who authorized it.

GM Guidance

Use the Collegium for heists, bureaucratic duels, rescue missions, industrial hazards, moral bargains, and the occasional journey into a damp impossible basement. Let competent people inside it be helpful. Let its cruelty arise from priorities, secrecy, class, and fear of consequences—not universal evil.

The Collegium can lose a case, suffer a scandal, miscalculate, split into factions, or need Byl and Lott. It should be formidable, never infallible.
